name: U2 Streets
reference: Where the Streets Have No Name: U2, The Joshua Tree (1987, prod. Brian Eno and Daniel Lanois)
rig: The Edge: Gibson Explorer / Fender Strat -> Vox AC30 Top Boost, with a dotted-eighth digital delay (Korg SDD-3000 era) that makes the sixteenth-note arpeggio
notes: Amp = Slammin Vox AC30 Top Boost, volume 5, cut 4, at the edge of breakup. Cab = '64 AC30 2x12 Blue Alnico (57 + R121 blend). The delay IS the part, so it is ON by default: 357 ms = a dotted eighth at ~126 BPM, feedback 0.45, bright (6.5 kHz), mix 40% so the repeats are nearly as loud as the dry, plus a short 480L Large Hall tail. SW8 LEAD turns that delay OFF (the boost slot is empty). Spread is on for width. Unconfirmed [verify]: the guitar and the delay unit on the record. Levels are unmeasured. Research: 80s-tones.md shortlist (captures and model ids checked with `tone3000.py models`).
